status: public House population projection; anchor examples do not replace canonical entity records
title: The Inhabited House — Society, Institutions and the Observable World
purpose: Populate the Potato House with concrete social reality so symbolic operators describe how real relations behave rather than becoming the subject matter themselves.
core_rule: Symbols and operators are grammar. People, organizations, traditions, technologies, territories, resources, laws, events and relationships are the population.

triune_lenses.label: Spirit / Meaning
triune_lenses.question: What makes this meaningful, legitimate, sacred, desirable, obligatory or worth preserving?
triune_lenses.caution: Spirit is a meaning/legitimation lens, not a claim that every institution has a literal supernatural spirit.

triune_lenses.label: Mind / Knowledge
triune_lenses.question: How does it perceive, remember, decide, coordinate, learn and communicate?
triune_lenses.caution: Mind is a coordination/knowledge lens. It does not imply organizations are literally conscious.

triune_lenses.label: Body / Matter
triune_lenses.question: What materially embodies it, who participates, and what resources or infrastructure let it act?
triune_lenses.caution: The internal repository spine calls this Matter / Observable World. 'Body' is the public triune projection emphasizing embodiment.

entity_contract: assets, budgets, infrastructure and material capacity

anchors.name: United Nations
anchors.summary: Founded in 1945; currently 193 Member States. It provides a forum where states deliberate, negotiate and coordinate under the UN Charter.
anchors.spirit: Charter purposes, international norms, legitimacy and shared problem-solving.
anchors.mind: General Assembly, Security Council, Secretariat, diplomacy, reporting and specialized knowledge systems.
anchors.body: 193 Member States, headquarters and offices, budgets, staff and operational programmes.

anchors.name: European Union
anchors.summary: A union of 27 Member States with shared institutions, bodies, agencies and a treaty-based legal order.
anchors.spirit: Treaties, shared legal-political commitments and European public purpose.
anchors.mind: Commission, Parliament, Council structures, courts, agencies, regulation and policy coordination.
anchors.body: 27 Member States, almost 450 million inhabitants, common budget, market and institutional infrastructure.

source.label: European Union — Key facts and figures

anchors.name: World Health Organization
anchors.summary: WHO coordinates international public-health work with 194 Member States across six regions.
anchors.spirit: Right-to-health principles, equity, public-health purpose and institutional values.
anchors.mind: Epidemiology, guidelines, health data, technical expertise, surveillance and programme coordination.
anchors.body: Member States, Secretariat, regional offices, country presence, staff and health programmes.

anchors.name: International Monetary Fund
anchors.summary: A global organization accountable to 191 member countries, focused on monetary cooperation and financial stability.
anchors.spirit: Cooperation, stability and stated prosperity objectives.
anchors.mind: Economic surveillance, policy analysis, statistics, technical assistance and lending frameworks.
anchors.body: 191 member countries, financial resources, staff, lending capacity and country programmes.

anchors.name: World Bank Group
anchors.summary: Five organizations working together on development through financing, knowledge and expertise.
anchors.spirit: Poverty reduction, shared prosperity and livable-planet development mission.
anchors.mind: Development research, project appraisal, country diagnostics, policy expertise and evaluation.
anchors.body: Five organizations, financial commitments, staff, country operations and funded projects.

source.label: World Bank Group — Who We Are

anchors.name: Bank for International Settlements
anchors.summary: Owned by 63 central banks and monetary authorities; provides a forum for central-bank cooperation and banking services to institutional partners.
anchors.spirit: Monetary and financial stability, cooperation and institutional trust.
anchors.mind: Research, committees, policy dialogue, statistics and financial-system analysis.
anchors.body: 63 member central banks/authorities, Basel headquarters, banking operations and Innovation Hub centres.

anchors.name: European Central Bank
anchors.summary: An official EU institution at the heart of the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism.
anchors.spirit: Price stability mandate, institutional independence and public monetary responsibility.
anchors.mind: Monetary analysis, policy decisions, banking supervision, statistics and economic research.
anchors.body: ECB staff, Governing Council, euro-area national central banks and supervisory infrastructure.

anchors.name: Danmarks Nationalbank
anchors.summary: Denmark's central bank, with objectives including stable prices, safe payments and a stable financial system.
anchors.spirit: Public monetary mandate and confidence in payments and financial stability.
anchors.mind: Economic analysis, monetary policy operations, payment oversight and financial-stability monitoring.
anchors.body: Central-bank balance sheet, payment infrastructure, staff, facilities and operational systems.

anchors.name: UNESCO
anchors.summary: Works across education, science, culture and information with 194 Member States.
anchors.spirit: Cultural diversity, peace, education, heritage and shared human knowledge.
anchors.mind: Standards, policy knowledge, research cooperation, education and information programmes.
anchors.body: Member States, field offices, national commissions, institutes, heritage and programme networks.

anchors.name: CERN
anchors.summary: A European particle-physics laboratory run by 25 Member States, with wider international participation.
anchors.spirit: Cooperative scientific inquiry and shared research infrastructure.
anchors.mind: Physics theory, experiments, engineering, computation and international scientific collaboration.
anchors.body: Accelerators, detectors, laboratories, computing infrastructure, staff and Member State funding.

anchors.name: International Committee of the Red Cross
anchors.summary: Provides protection and assistance to people affected by armed conflict and other violence and promotes international humanitarian law.
anchors.spirit: Humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence and protection of dignity.
anchors.mind: Humanitarian law, field assessment, protection work, negotiation, tracing and operational coordination.
anchors.body: Field offices in more than 90 countries, staff, logistics, medical assistance and relief operations.

anchors.name: Wikimedia Foundation
anchors.summary: Hosts and protects Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects while supporting volunteer communities and free knowledge.
anchors.spirit: Free knowledge, broad participation and long-term public access.
anchors.mind: Editorial communities, software, governance, moderation, curation and knowledge organization.
anchors.body: Servers, technical infrastructure, staff, grants and a global volunteer/movement network.

anchors.name: Linux Foundation
anchors.summary: Provides a neutral organizational home and infrastructure for open-source technology projects and communities.
anchors.spirit: Open collaboration, shared technology and ecosystem stewardship.
anchors.mind: Standards, governance, project coordination, training, research and software collaboration.
anchors.body: Hosted projects, contributor networks, member organizations, funding and technical/operational infrastructure.

anchors.name: ASML
anchors.summary: Designs and manufactures lithography hardware, software and services used by chipmakers to mass-produce microchips.
anchors.spirit: Corporate purpose, engineering culture and innovation priorities.
anchors.mind: Optics, mechatronics, software, computational lithography, metrology and R&D knowledge.
anchors.body: Lithography systems, factories, supply chain, employees, service network and customer fabs.

anchors.name: A.P. Moller - Maersk
anchors.summary: A global logistics company whose history runs from steam shipping through containerization to integrated logistics.
anchors.spirit: Commercial purpose, service norms and organizational identity around connecting trade.
anchors.mind: Routing, scheduling, logistics planning, data, customs and supply-chain coordination.
anchors.body: Ships, terminals, warehouses, containers, trucks, contracts, employees and global routes.

anchors.name: Novo Nordisk
anchors.summary: A Denmark-headquartered healthcare company focused on chronic diseases including diabetes and obesity.
anchors.spirit: Health mission, corporate values and stated patient focus.
anchors.mind: Biomedical research, clinical development, data, regulatory knowledge and manufacturing know-how.
anchors.body: Medicines, production sites, laboratories, employees, distribution and healthcare partnerships.

page_note: This is a seed population, not a complete world model. The long-term atlas should expand through canonical country/entity records and typed edges rather than turning the House page into a giant catalog.
